newsitem.title: FRANCE: NATO, Russia sign "Founding Act" partnership deal.
newsitem.headline: NATO, Russia sign "Founding Act" partnership deal.

text.p: The leaders of Russia and the NATO alliance signed the "Founding Act" of a new partnership for security in Europe at a ceremony in Paris on Tuesday.

The Founding Act on Mutual Relations is designed to bind Russia into efforts to create a new European security order and ease the 16-nation alliance's eastward expansion by admitting some of Moscow's former communist allies.

Russian President Boris Yeltsin and NATO Secretary-General Javier Solana were the first to sign the document in the ornate banqueting hall of the Elysee presidential palace, applauded by U.S. President Bill Clinton and French President Jacques Chirac.

The accord creates a NATO-Russia council for consultation on European security and enshrines close military and political cooperation between Moscow and the 16-nation Atlantic alliance, giving Russia a voice, but not a veto, in allied decisions.
When the document was placed in front of Yeltsin, he gave a mock sigh before breaking into a broad grin and signing. After appending his signature, he wiggled the pen.
When all 16 NATO leaders had signed, Yeltsin and Solana exchanged documents and embraced each other to applause.
